verdicts.reason: A: the suitcase is so large it outweighs the headline. The CTA is a tiny pill whose label is barely legible, and the logo has been demoted to the bottom corner, crammed beside the sunglasses on top of a blue circle cropped by the edge. Its headline and subhead at least stay grouped. B shares the tiny CTA, the logo and sunglasses jammed onto the cropped circle, and the demoted brand, and adds new problems: a large gap cuts the subhead off from the headline, and a big dead band sits between the CTA and the footer, so the layout feels scattered.
